subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: What native memory trust contract should OpenClaw adopt for durable memory across memory-core, QMD/session memory, Active Memory, Memory Wiki, and plugin SDK surfaces?
rationale: The evidence shows a real security and session-state gap, but automation cannot choose the permanent trust axes, default enforcement mode, migration behavior, or native-vs-plugin boundary safely.

options.title: Define native trust contract first
options.body: Create a maintainer-approved design that covers source, reviewed_by, influence_state, expiry, storage policy, influence policy, backend persistence, and migration before code changes.

options.title: Fold into provenance MVP
options.body: Make #42647 the schema/provenance prerequisite and keep #7707 as the security acceptance criteria for trust-aware retrieval and review gates.

options.title: Externalize to plugin or MCP
options.body: Treat trust-rich memory as optional outside core only if maintainers explicitly accept that default OpenClaw memory remains source-only.

recommendation.title: Define native trust contract first
recommendation.body: Create a maintainer-approved design that covers source, reviewed_by, influence_state, expiry, storage policy, influence policy, backend persistence, and migration before code changes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available owner signal for memory host contracts, memory-core plugin seams, and the prior maintainer review on this issue.
